title: Ephemeral-proxy transition for persistent socket migrations during active-active traffic shifts
creator: Marcela Ortega
description:
Goal: implement an ephemeral proxy transition layer that enables minimal-disruption migration of long-lived connections (WebSocket / HTTP/2 streaming / gRPC bidi) when we perform active-active traffic redistribution between regions or gateways. The approach should preserve conversational continuity where possible, respect p99 latency and availability SLOs, and integrate with existing circuit breaker and load-shedding policies. This ticket covers design, prototype, canary rollout plan, and automated validation harnesses.

Background: Current region cutovers and traffic rebalancing cause a large fraction of persistent connections to drop and reconnect, resulting in user-perceived interruptions and regressed SLOs for streaming workloads. Existing strategies either rely on clients reconnecting (causes state loss and higher tail latency) or complex global session replication (operationally heavy). The ephemeral-proxy approach introduces a short-lived in-path proxy that brokers the handoff between origin and target gateways, buffering inflight data and coordinating a seamless switch when possible.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by SRE and Runtime teams
Prototype handles WebSocket and HTTP/2 stream handoffs with < 500ms median additional latency and <1% error rate under load profile A
Canary rollout in us-west with traffic shaping shows no more than 5% p99 latency regression and preserves at least 90% of in-flight streams without reconnects
Circuit breaker integration triggers fallback paths when target region capacity under pressure (configurable thresholds) and metrics emitted for every fallback event
Automated chaos tests (region drain, node kill, network partition) demonstrate graceful degradation and meet SLO guardrails defined in the release plan
Docs and SDK guidance published for client reconnect behavior and recommended backoff strategies
tasks: Draft design doc: ephemeral proxy handshake, token exchange, sequence checkpointing, buffer management (owner: Aisha)
Implement prototype proxy in edge control plane with pluggable backpressure policy (owner: Rui Chen)
Add telemetry: per-connection handoff duration, buffer occupancy, bytes re-transmitted, fallback reason codes (owner: DataInfra)
Build simulation harness to replay production streaming traces and validate handoff success rates under realistic load (owner: SRE)
Integrate with circuit breaker service: define thresholds and expose API to trigger immediate drain/fallback (owner: Platform)
End-to-end tests: WebSocket, HTTP/2, gRPC bidi scenarios with and without KV-cache priming (owner: QA)
Canary rollout plan and runbook: staged percentages, telemetry alerts, automated rollback hooks (owner: Ops)
Client SDK guidance and minor client patch for graceful resume token handling (owner: SDK)
Security review: ensure ephemeral tokens and audit logs meet compliance (owner: Security)
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, SRE, Platform and SDK teams. Agreed on handshake primitives and minimal token format.
2026-03-04: Prototype skeleton pushed to github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/tree/ephemeral-handoff (WIP). Basic buffering implemented for WebSocket text frames.
2026-03-06: SRE requested metrics for buffer latency and rebuffer count. Added telemetry tags to correlate by customer and model route.
2026-03-08: Design review feedback: avoid synchronous global KV calls during handoff; instead use lease-based checkpoint publish. Updated doc accordingly.

2026-03-09: QA ran first simulation: 78% of streams preserved for a medium load trace; identified pathological case when buffer > 10MB causing memory spikes. Added max-buffer policy and spill-to-disk fallback.
2026-03-10: Security review requested short-lived HMAC tokens (TTL 60s) and audit log entries for every accepted handoff. Blocking on HSM key quota for signing; Ops ticket opened.
notes:
Trade-offs considered: full session replication vs ephemeral proxy. Chosen approach minimizes cross-region writes and keeps operational complexity low but adds transient resource pressure at the edge; mitigations include strict buffer caps, spill-to-disk with size limits, and aggressive load-shedding when circuit-breaker thresholds are hit.

Open questions: optimal HMAC TTL for tokens balancing replay risk vs handshake latency; whether to pre-warm KV cache on target for hot sessions or rely on prefix caching. Plan to run a controlled experiment comparing both under production-like traffic.
rollback_plan: Immediate disablement of ephemeral proxy via feature flag routing (edge-config). On rollback, clients revert to normal reconnect path. Monitoring runbook: alert on >3x reconnect rate compared to baseline, activate incident channel, and reintroduce traffic at 1% increments after post-mortem.
operational_playbook: 1) Monitor handoff.success_rate, handoff.latency_p99, reconnect.rate; 2) If handoff.success_rate < 80% for 5m, pause cutover and increase drain time; 3) If buffer.memory_pressure > 85% or node swap rate increases, enable spill-to-disk and reduce canary percent; 4) If target region circuit-breaker trips, route fallback to reconnect path and emit fault-reason metrics
qa_plan: Fuzzed connection migrations, deterministic replays of 10K connections with mixed message sizes, memory/CPU leak checks, and chaos testing (node kill, network loss). Define pass criteria for 95th-percentile latency additions and state preservation rate.
final_notes: This ticket is the foundation for broader active-active resilience for streaming products. Once validated, we will generalize the ephemeral proxy primitives into a reusable library for Dedicated and Private deployments.
